Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

since conjunction

because, seeing that

also as (because), seeing that, now that, given that, inasmuch as

classical

Cic. Clu. 123: quae cum ita sint (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.54: quī cum ūnā domō jam capī nōn possint, in aliās domōs … exeunt

cum (+ subjunctive)

conjunction, with the subjunctive

since, as

The reason given as the circumstance: “since, as”. Praesertim cum, all the more since. Quae cum ita sint, since this is so.

Other words

  • quoniam — since, now that

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Varr. RR 2.3.1: quoniam satis bālāstī

    A reason both speakers know or can see.

  • quandōquidem — since indeed, seeing that

    conjunction, with the indicative · also used · classical · Ter. And. 3.5.2: quandōquidem tam iners, tam nūllī cōnsilī sum (Lewis & Short); Cic. Brut. 163 (Lewis & Short)

    A stronger “since”, with a shade of “if that is how it is”.

  • sīquidem — if indeed, if it is true that; and so, since

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 688: et causa jūsta est, sīquidem ita est ut praedicās; Cic. Fam. 9.12.1: grātulor Bajīs nostrīs, sī quidem, ut scrībis, salūbrēs repente factae sunt (Lewis & Short)

    Also written sī quidem. It grants the condition for the sake of the argument, which is how it comes to mean “since”.

Examples

  • quī cum ūnā domō jam capī nōn possint, in aliās domōs tamquam in colōniās exeunt

    since they can no longer fit in one house, they go out to other houses, as if to coloniesCic. Off. 1.54

  • cui Cossinius: quoniam satis bālāstī, inquit, ō Faustule noster

    to whom Cossinius said: “since you have bleated enough, our dear Faustulus”Varr. RR 2.3.1

  • dē pāvōnibus, inquit, līberē licet dīcās, quoniam discessit Fircellius

    “you may speak freely about peacocks,” he said, “now that Fircellius has gone”Varr. RR 3.6.1

  • posteāquam (+ indic.)

    now thatTraupman 352

  • et causa jūsta est, sīquidem ita est ut praedicās

    and you have a good case, if indeed it is as you sayPlaut. Aul. 688

See also because, for.
